title: Quantification of protein-protein interactions in highly denatured whey and potato protein gels
author: Tanger, Andlinger, et al.

steps.title: Prepare Buffer B1
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.05 mol L⁻¹ NaH₂PO₄/Na₂HPO₄ in de‑ionised water, adjust the pH to 7.0, and bring the final volume to the desired amount. No SDS or DTT are added.

steps.title: Prepare Buffer B2
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.05 mol L⁻¹ NaH₂PO₄/Na₂HPO₄ and 2 g L⁻¹ sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) in de‑ionised water, adjust the pH to 7.0, and bring to the final volume. No DTT is added.

steps.title: Prepare Buffer B3
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.05 mol L⁻¹ NaH₂PO₄/Na₂HPO₄, 2 g L⁻¹ SDS and 1.5 g L⁻¹ dithiothreitol (DTT) in de‑ionised water, adjust the pH to 7.0, and bring to the final volume.

steps.title: Note Buffer Concentrations
steps.instruction: The SDS and DTT concentrations are higher than in the original Keim & Hinrichs method to ensure complete dissolution of strongly bound proteins; concentrations above 10 g L⁻¹ SDS were tested but caused filament formation and were not used.

steps.title: Prepare Gel Samples
steps.instruction: Make three gel types as follows:

substeps.instruction: Whey protein gel A: dissolve whey protein to 15 % (w/w) in water, adjust to pH 7, heat for 30 min at 85 °C.
Whey protein gel B: dissolve whey protein to 15 % (w/w), adjust to pH 5, heat for 30 min at 70 °C.
Potato protein gel: dissolve potato protein to 10 % (w/w), adjust to pH 7, heat for 30 min at 70 °C.

steps.title: Take Replicate Portions
steps.instruction: From each gel, cut six independent portions (six‑fold replication) to be used for the solubility measurements.

steps.title: Dissolve Gels in Buffers
steps.instruction: For each replicate, add an appropriate amount of gel to each of the three buffers (B1, B2, B3) and mix until the gel is fully dispersed.

steps.title: Centrifuge Suspensions
steps.instruction: Centrifuge each tube at 10 000 g for 20 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Collect Supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully decant the supernatant without disturbing the pellet; this supernatant contains the solubilised nitrogen.

steps.title: Determine Nitrogen by Dumas
steps.instruction: Measure the total nitrogen content of each supernatant using a Dumas combustion analyser according to the instrument’s standard protocol.

steps.title: Calculate Interaction Fractions
steps.instruction: Apply equations (1)–(7) supplied in the original study to the nitrogen values obtained from buffers B1, B2 and B3 to obtain the relative contributions of electrostatic, hydrophobic and disulfide interactions.

steps.title: Optional SDS‑PAGE on B2 Supernatant
steps.instruction: Run non‑reducing and reducing SDS‑PAGE gels with the supernatant obtained from buffer B2 to detect small oligomers that remain soluble after centrifugation.

steps.title: Optional Analyse Pellet from B3
steps.instruction: If any pellet remains after treatment with buffer B3, dissolve the pellet in SDS‑PAGE loading buffer and run a gel to check for uncleaved bonds (e.g., isopeptide bonds) or insufficient DTT concentration.
